procedures_performed: CBC with differential, blood culture, electrolytes, BUN, and creatinine, glucose, UA, and urine culture all were ordered.
Chest x-ray was ordered as well with 2 views to evaluate for a possible pneumonia.
Pulse oximetry checks were ordered every shift and as needed with O2 ordered per nasal cannula if O2 saturations were less that 94%.
Gave D5 and quarter of normal saline at 45 mL per hour, which was just slightly above maintenance rate to help with hydration.
He was doing clear liquids well and so I saline locked to help to accommodate improve the mobility with the patient.

diagnosis_explanation: Your child had an ear infection in both ears. This is called bilateral otitis media. Your child also had a fever.
medication_rationale:
Tylenol as needed:
This medicine helps reduce your child's fever. It can also help with pain. Your child may feel better and more comfortable. This is a sign the medicine is working. Call your doctor if your child's fever does not get better or is very high.

Ibuprofen as needed:
This medicine helps lower your child's fever. It can also help with pain. Your child may feel more comfortable. This means the medicine is working. Call your doctor if your child's fever does not get better or is very high.

Ceftriaxone 500 mg once daily:
This medicine is an antibiotic. It fights the germs causing your child's ear infection. It may also help if your child has a serious infection. Your child will receive this medicine through an IV. It helps treat the ear infection and a possible blood infection. Call your doctor if your child develops a rash or has trouble breathing.

Albuterol Aerosols every 6 hours:
This medicine helps your child's breathing. It opens up the airways in the lungs. Your child may breathe easier after using this medicine. This means the medicine is working. Call your doctor if your child's breathing does not get better or gets worse.

Omnicef 125 mg/5 mL once daily:
This medicine is an antibiotic. It fights the germs causing your child's ear infection. Your child will take this medicine by mouth. It helps treat the ear infection. Call your doctor if your child develops a rash or has severe diarrhea.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- Your child may feel tired and have less energy. This is normal.
- Keep your child on clear liquids for now.
- Do not lift your child more than 10 pounds.
- Your child should be breathing comfortably.
- Watch for any return of fever or fast breathing.
- Your child’s goal this week is to drink 4 cups of clear liquids.
- Call your doctor if your child has trouble breathing.

**Week 2:**
- Your child may start to feel a little more playful.
- You can slowly add soft foods to your child’s diet.
- Avoid heavy lifting for your child.
- Watch for any signs of ear pain or fussiness.
- Your child’s goal this week is to eat soft foods without problems.
- Call your doctor if your child develops a fever again.

**Week 3:**
- Your child may have more energy for short playtimes.
- Gradually increase the variety of foods your child eats.
- You can start carrying your child for short distances.
- Your child should be breathing well and without effort.
- Your child’s goal this week is to play for 15 minutes at a time.
- Call your doctor if your child seems to be in pain.

**Week 4:**
- Your child should be back to most normal activities.
- You can slowly return to normal feeding for your child.
- Your child may resume normal carrying and playing.
- Watch for any ear discomfort or hearing changes.
- Your child’s goal this week is to play as usual.
- Call your doctor if your child’s breathing changes.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Most children feel much better within 2 to 4 weeks.
- Continue to offer soft foods as needed for comfort.
- Keep fluids regular to stay well hydrated.
- Follow up with your doctor as recommended.
- Watch for any signs of ear infection returning.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Your child cannot breathe: Call 911 right away.
- Your child is unresponsive: This needs emergency help now.
- Your child has a seizure: Call 911 right away.
- Your child is bleeding badly: Bleeding will not stop.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Your child has a fever over 101 F: This needs checking now.
- Your child's ear looks worse: Redness or pus is seen.
- Your child cannot keep fluids down: They may get too sick.
- Your child is too sleepy: They do not wake easily.
- Your child has neck stiffness: This needs ER care now.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Your child has mild ear pain: Pain is getting better.
- Your child has a small rash: No large spots are seen.
- Your child needs medicine refills: Ask the office nurse.
- You have questions about medicine: Call the doctor's office.
